instructions: Rinse the anchovies in cold water. Pull off the heads (the guts usually come out with them), then pat the fish very dry with paper towels.
Stir the flour and the 2 tsp salt together on a plate. Coat each anchovy in the flour and shake off the extra.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat until a pinch of flour sizzles at once, about 1/2 inch deep.
Fry the anchovies in small batches, 1 to 2 minutes per side, until golden. Don't crowd the pan.
Transfer each batch to a paper towel and sprinkle with flaky salt. Cut the lemon into wedges and serve with the anchovies right away.
method_notes: Spanish Food Guide's version (25 minutes, no rating shown) leads as a fallback: salted flour, about 1/2 inch of olive oil, roughly a minute a side. Julia's Cuisine fries 2 to 3 minutes a side in vegetable oil, so the time is written as 1 to 2. Both serve with lemon; the baguette in the lead was left out. Fresh anchovies are often sold cleaned, which saves most of the prep time. One pound is the sources' portion for four.
